text.p: Construction group Leighton Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it would purchase the Visionstream unit of government-owned telecommunications carrier, Telstra Australia, for an undisclosed sum.
Visionstream was formed in 1994 to design, install, commission and maintain the co-axial portion of Telstra's broadband network.
Leighton said the service contract for the continued roll-out of Telstra's broadbased network associated with the Visionstream sale was valued at around A$300 million.

Leighton chief executive, Wal King, said the acquisition of Visionstream was in line with the group's growth strategy of developing new businesses that complemented the existing skills within the Group.

"Telecommunications and related businesses will continue to generate good opportunities, and we will provide Visionstream with the necessary resources to further enhance its commercial, contracting and business development capabilities," King said.
Visionstream's 2,000 employees are to be retained under existing enterprise bargaining agreements while a board of directors comprising Leighton and Visionstream executives would be established.
Visionstream also provides installation for the Foxtel pay television service owned by Telstra and News Corp Ltd.
Leighton is 46 percent owned by Germany's Hochtief Ag.
By 3.15 p.m. (0415 GMT), Leighton shares were 15 cents higher at A$5.46 on turnover of 216,570 shares.
